title: Dow, S&P and Nasdaq Rise as Oil Retreats and Tesla Jumps on Upgrade
excerpt: Stocks climbed Monday, Oct. 26, as cooling oil prices and Anthropic's IPO filing lifted technology shares ahead of the Fed decision and a heavy week of big-tech earnings.
body:
• U.S. stocks rose Monday, Oct. 26: by midday the Nasdaq was up 1.22% to 26,271, the S&P 500 up 0.91% to 7,693 and the Dow up 0.31% to 52,379.
  • Tesla jumped about 6% intraday after Barclays upgraded the stock to overweight, with analyst Dan Levy raising his price target to $450 from $370.
  • Crude oil eased after hitting a near six-month high last week, helping sentiment ahead of a heavy earnings week.
  • Investors face the Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday and September PCE inflation and third-quarter GDP data on Thursday, with about a third of the S&P 500 reporting earnings this week.

U.S. stocks rose on Monday as crude oil retreated from a near six-month high and a public filing for Anthropic's initial public offering lifted artificial intelligence shares, ahead of a week dominated by big technology earnings and the Federal Reserve's rate decision. By 11:31 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite was up 1.22% to 26,271, the S&P 500 had climbed 0.91% to 7,693 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average was 0.31% higher at 52,379, according to The Motley Fool's midday market data.

Futures had pointed to a steadier open. At 7:05 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 193 points, or 0.37%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 0.07% and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 0.06%, Reuters reported.

Oil Retreat Helps, Anthropic Filing Lifts AI Stocks

Crude oil prices eased after hitting a near six-month high last week. On Sunday, Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States, Reuters reported. The slight decline in crude helped support the S&P 500 amid easing global inflation concerns, The Motley Fool reported.

AI-linked stocks rose after Anthropic revealed its IPO paperwork on Monday. Nvidia added nearly 3%, Microsoft and Amazon gained nearly 1% each, Micron rose 3%, and AMD and Broadcom gained 2.5% and 3% respectively, Reuters reported. The broader Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was up over 3%. CoreWeave rose 5.7% and Nebius Group rose 2.3%, reversing earlier losses that followed comments by SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk about funding for neocloud companies.

"Strong AI demand alone may no longer be enough. Markets want evidence of monetization, margins and cash flow."

— Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist, Saxo

Tesla Rallies on Barclays Upgrade

Tesla was among the day's biggest movers. The stock rose 1.9% in premarket trading after Barclays upgraded its rating to "overweight" from "equal-weight," Reuters reported, and it extended those gains during the session to about $394.51, up about 6%, by 12:25 p.m. ET, according to The Motley Fool. Barclays analyst Dan Levy raised his price target on Tesla to $450 from $370, The Motley Fool reported. Tesla had come under pressure after its results last week, Reuters noted.

Elsewhere, Surgery Partners soared 46% after confirming it will be acquired for approximately $5.7 billion, while Brazil-linked shares fell after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term on Sunday in a result that defied polls. The iShares Brazil ETF slumped almost 26% and MercadoLibre traded nearly 10% lower, according to Reuters and The Motley Fool. Gold was up 0.73% to $4,037.10 by midday and the 10-year Treasury yield was up to 5.00%, with real estate the leading sector and healthcare the primary loser, The Motley Fool reported.

Earnings and the Fed Dominate the Week Ahead

About one-third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon.com, whose results will be closely watched for signs that heavy AI investments are paying off, Reuters reported. Most megacap and growth stocks gained Monday after the S&P 500 posted losses for the last two weeks.

The Fed's rate decision is due on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected after its September hike. Traders still see a December hike as firmly possible, and at least two 25-basis-point increases by mid-2027, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. Both the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index for September, and third-quarter GDP, expected to show 3.2% growth, are due on Thursday. Investors are also monitoring the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the U.S. Congress.
